problems.source_says: The two pools are ChatGPT output with no participant and human ideas written without AI, so no person produced a scored idea with AI available. The reconciled c010 form codes the same Experiment 2B ChatGPT-only versus Human-only comparison 'mixed' (S3-O4, S3-O5), and the c010 outcome check confirmed that code. The two forms share this sample, so they should agree. With 'yes' and construct 'diversity', the codebook rule in section 1 gives across_people, which contradicts the form's own question 'none'. Fix: 'mixed', as in c010. The question 'none', the comparison 'ai_vs_human', the direction and the numbers stand.
problems.quote: In the extreme case of study 2b (suggesting a toy for a seven-year-old child using a brick and a fan), only 6% of the AI-generated ideas (ChatGPT-only) were unique, compared with 100% of human ideas.
problems.locator: PDF p. 2 (journal p. 1108), right column, first paragraph; c010 form, S3-O4 and S3-O5; codebook section 1; form-spec, Field notes, 'question'

confirmed: Every outcome is computed on the ideas, and none is self-reported. The unique fraction comes from pairwise cosine similarity of the ideas' Universal Sentence Encoder embeddings (S1-O1 to S6-O1, S3-O2). S2-O2 counts the ideas that contain the word 'sprinkler' (PDF p. 1, journal p. 1107, right column, last two paragraphs; PDF p. 2, p. 1108, left column below Fig. 1).

ChatGPT was available in the same session while every treated idea was written ('idea sets created in each of their experiments with the aid of ChatGPT'). So ai_available 'yes', timing 'immediate' and question 'across_people' follow the codebook rule for S1-O1, S2-O1, S2-O2, S3-O1, S4-O1, S5-O1 and S6-O1. No idea is produced after AI is removed, so no after_ai record is missing (PDF p. 1, p. 1107, right column; codebook section 1).

The diversity construct compares different people. The paper says each participant submitted one idea, and the per-condition n in the online Supplementary Table 1 add up to the people analyzed: Experiment 1, 130 + 103 = 233; 2a, 100 + 96 + 95 = 291; 2b, 98 + 102 = 200 plus 100 ChatGPT-only; 3, 95 + 99 = 194; 4, 88 + 110 + 114 + 88 = 400. Caveat for the record: Lee and Chung's Experiment 1 let participants type several ideas into one box (about 1.69 each), so an Experiment 1 'idea' here is one participant's entry (PDF p. 1, p. 1107, left column; SI pp. 3-6; c010 PDF p. 6, journal p. 1911, Methods, Experiment 1).

Unit 'set' is the paper's own unit. Fig. 1 gives one unique fraction per condition with '95% confidence intervals for individual proportions', and the SI compares condition pools with a proportions z-test. Unit 'output' fits S2-O2, a count of ideas coded for one word (PDF p. 2, Fig. 1 legend; SI p. 2, Supplementary Table 1 legend; PDF p. 1, p. 1107, right column).

Every 'reported' number matches the PDF. In the text layer of PDF p. 2, each Fig. 1 value label sits over its own bar label: Experiment 1 web search 0.96, ChatGPT 0.74; 2a Human 0.92, web search 0.91, ChatGPT 0.70; 2b Human-only 1.00, ChatGPT–human 0.41, ChatGPT-only 0.06; 3 web search 1.00, ChatGPT 0.88; 4 web search low 1.00, high 0.99, ChatGPT low 0.94, high 0.93; 5 web search base 0.98, high 0.98, ChatGPT high 0.63, base 0.59. The sprinkler counts (20 of 96, 7, 12), the 6% versus 100% sentence and 'Build-a-Breeze Castle' match PDF pp. 1-2.

The online Supplementary Table 1 (not in this PDF) confirms the form's arms and directions. Its 'GPT-aided' 41.2% is the Fig. 1 'ChatGPT–human' bar. Its Experiment 4 and 5 tests are the within-level cell contrasts the form codes. Both Experiment 4 tests are non-significant after Bonferroni correction (p = 0.096, 0.132), so no_clear_difference holds. Both Experiment 5 tests have p < 0.001. 37 of the 45 robustness comparisons are significant, as the form says (SI pp. 2-8, https://static-content.springer.com/esm/art%3A10.1038%2Fs41562-025-02173-x/MediaObjects/41562_2025_2173_MOESM1_ESM.pdf).

The SI has no test of ChatGPT-only versus Human-only. Its second Experiment 2b test is GPT-only versus GPT-aided (6% vs 41.2%, z = 5.873), so S3-O2 rests on the Fig. 1 values and the text, as coded (SI pp. 4-5).

The SI's Experiment 2a arm sizes (ChatGPT 96, web search 100, Human-only 95) turn the sprinkler counts into shares of 20.8, 7.0 and 12.6 percent. So S2-O2's treatment_lower holds on shares, not only on raw counts (SI pp. 3-4; PDF p. 1, p. 1107, right column).

Measure codes fit codebook section 6: embedding_similarity for the Universal Sentence Encoder threshold measure. lexical_overlap is defensible for the S2-O2 word-presence count, and category_count would also fit (PDF p. 1, p. 1107, right column).

The robustness variants (thresholds 0.75 and 0.85, centroid similarity, pairwise similarity, minimum-spanning-tree distance) sit in measure_detail, as form-spec rule 7 asks. The paper presents them as supplementary analyses of the same diversity outcome (PDF p. 2, p. 1108, left column; SI p. 2).

No outcome that bears on the three questions is missing. The paper restates Lee and Chung's average-creativity result without numbers. The Fig. 1 ChatGPT–human versus ChatGPT-only contrast (0.41 vs 0.06) compares AI-assisted people with AI alone and answers none of the three questions (PDF p. 1, p. 1107, left column; PDF p. 2, Fig. 1).

Primary 'paper_primary' for S1-O1 to S6-O1 matches 'In our primary analysis' and the 0.8 threshold of the paper's 'main analysis'. S2-O2 and S3-O2 are correctly secondary (PDF p. 1, p. 1107, right column; PDF p. 2, p. 1108, left column).
S3-O2's question 'none' and comparison 'ai_vs_human' follow the form-spec field note on 'question' (form-spec, Field notes).

The Reporting Summary adds no outcome. It calls the work a 'Secondary analysis of previously published data by Lee & Chung (2024)' and gives N/A for sample, exclusions and randomization. PDF pp. 6-10 are blank template sections (PDF pp. 4-10).
summary: Every outcome is computed on the ideas, the question, construct and unit codes follow the codebook, every reported number matches Fig. 1 and the text exactly, and the online Supplementary Table 1 confirms the form's arms, contrasts and directions. The coding is refuted on one point: S3-O2 codes AI availability 'yes' for a ChatGPT-only versus Human-only comparison that the reconciled c010 form codes 'mixed' on the same sample, and 'yes' with a diversity construct would give across_people under the codebook rule, not the form's 'none'.
